To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
γ-ray irradiation can be used to prepare highly pressure-sensitive graphene sponge for piezoresistance sensor.
γ-ray irradiation can be used for the mild, residual-free, and controllable graphene reduction process to prepare graphene sponge with excellent physical properties and high pressure sensitivity.
a highly pressure-sensitive graphene sponge is fabricated by γ-ray reduction and used as the sensing material for a piezoresisttive pressure sensor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a highly sensitive, stable, and low pressure detection limit piezoresistivity sensor based on γ-ray irradiation-reduced graphene sponge.

the development of a novel, highly pressure-sensitive graphene sponge with a gauge factor of ~1.03 kpa–1, pressure detection limit of ~10 Pa, and high stress retention (76%) after 800 cycles compressing/relasation at strain of ~50%, by γ-ray irradiated reduction of graphene oxide (GO).
the fabrication of a highly pressure-sensitive GS by γ-ray irradiated method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the γ-ray irradiation induced reduction of graphene sponge (GS) offers a highly sensitive pressure sensor with low pressure detection limit of tens of Pascals.
the γ-ray irradiation induced reduction of graphene oxide (GO) is an efficient and controllable approach to prepare highly pressure-sensitive graphene sponge.
the γ-ray irradiation method offers a facile, clean, and controllable way to fabricate the GS, which is a promising candidate material for pressure sensors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a highly pressure-sensitive, mechanically stable and low compression stress graphene sponge is fabricated by γ-ray radiation reduction.
the γ-ray irradiation method can effectively reduce graphene oxide and produce highly pressure-sensitive graphene sponge.

we have developed a new method to fabricate a highly pressure-sensitive GS by the γ-ray irradiation, and the pressure-sensitive GS has shown a high gauge factor of 103 kPa–1 and a low pressure detection limit of ~10 Pa, and the pressure sensor based on the GS shows excellent stability and durability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

γ-ray irradiation provides a mild, residue-free, and controllable method for fabricating graphene sponge with high sensitivity, low detection limit, and high stability for piezoresistance pressure sensors.

the γ-ray irradiation provides an efficient, clean, and mild method for the reduction of graphene oxide (GO), and the resultant graphene sponge exhibits excellent mechanical and electrical properties for the pressure-sensitive sensor.
a highly pressure-sensitive graphene sponge (GS) can be fabricated by γ-ray reduction.
